project.title: Choose project
project.description: One entry is created per project. Every template of the project becomes its own device.

reauth_confirm.title: New API token

reconfigure.title: Change connection

error.host_unreachable: {host} cannot be reached from Home Assistant ({detail}). Check address, network/VLAN and firewall.
error.connection_lost: The connection to {host} was interrupted ({detail}). Check whether http/https is right and try again.
error.not_semaphore: No Semaphore UI answers at {url} (HTTP {status}: {detail}). Check address, port and sub path, without "/api" at the end.
error.project_not_found: The project does not exist at {url} (any more), or this token may not see it (HTTP 404).
error.invalid_auth: The API token was rejected (HTTP 401). Create a new one in Semaphore under your user name → "API tokens" and check that it was copied completely.
error.no_projects: No project is visible with this token.
error.login_failed: Sign-in not possible: user name or password are wrong, or signing in with a password is switched off in Semaphore.
error.mfa_required: This user needs a second factor. That is not possible here - create the token in Semaphore and enter it.

init.title: Semaphore UI
init.description: While a task is running the integration polls every 5 seconds automatically.

data.check_for_updates: Check for new Semaphore version (asks GitHub every 6 h)
data.allow_parallel_runs: Allow starting again (start a template although a run of it is queued or running)
data.renew_token: Replace the API token by itself before it expires
data.token_days: Replace / warn when fewer than ... days are left
data.clear_login: Remove the stored user name and password
data.live_updates: Live updates while a task runs (WebSocket)
data.keep_recent: Keep templates visible for 24 hours after a run

data_description.allow_parallel_runs: Off (default): while a run of a template is queued or running, start and dry run are blocked - card, button and action. On: Home Assistant starts anyway; Semaphore queues the run or starts it in parallel (depending on "Allow parallel tasks" of the template). If the template allows parallel tasks in Semaphore, this always applies.
data_description.templates: Only ticked templates get devices, entities and schedule switches. Unticked ones are removed when you save (their dashboard cards then show a missing device); runs and schedules in Semaphore are not touched, and the counters of the project card count only the ticked ones. New templates from Semaphore show up automatically. At least one must stay ticked.
data_description.renew_token: On (default): when the token expires soon, the integration creates a new one with the token itself (same lifetime), checks it and switches over. The old token stays in Semaphore and expires by itself - you may still use it elsewhere. A token without an expiry date is left alone. Off: a notice with “Fix” appears under “Repairs” instead.
data_description.token_days: At most half of the lifetime of the token.
data_description.renew_username: Only needed when Semaphore already rejects a token (expired or deleted): the integration then signs in, creates a new token and signs out again. The sign-in is checked when you save. A second factor is not possible.
data_description.renew_password: It is not shown again; leaving it empty keeps the stored password. It is stored - like the token - encrypted.
data_description.clear_login: Tick and save: the user name and password are deleted.
data_description.live_updates: On (default): while a task runs, Home Assistant keeps a connection to Semaphore open. Status and the running step show up at once instead of at the next poll. No connection exists while nothing runs. If it does not work, polling simply continues.
data_description.keep_recent: Off (default): nothing changes. On: the sensor "Card visible" stays on for 24 hours after a run (until it is marked as done or a new run starts), even if nothing needs doing. Use it as the visibility condition of a card; the template card can hide itself with it.

error.no_templates: At least one template must stay ticked.
error.login_incomplete: For the emergency sign-in you need a user name and a password.
error.login_failed: Sign-in not possible: user name or password are wrong, or signing in with a password is switched off in Semaphore.
error.mfa_required: This user needs a second factor. That is not possible here - create the token in Semaphore and enter it.
error.login_unreachable: The sign-in could not be checked because Semaphore does not answer. Please save again later.

run_template.name: Run template
run_template.description: Starts a template in Semaphore. With "Wait" the finished report (start, duration, result, failure reason) is returned as the response.

wait.name: Wait
wait.description: Wait for the task to end and return the complete report.

timeout.name: Timeout
timeout.description: Maximum time to wait (seconds). Afterwards the current state is returned with timed_out: true.

message.name: Note
message.description: Note that is shown on the task in Semaphore.

limit.name: Limit
limit.description: Only these hosts (Ansible --limit), separate several with a comma.

raise_on_failure.name: Fail on error
raise_on_failure.description: Raise an error if the task fails (stops a script).

survey.name: Survey variables
survey.description: Values of the survey variables as name: value, e.g. target: dockerhost. Missing values use the default of the template, required ones without a value raise an error. Enum: value or label, select: list, secret: only possible here.

build_version.name: Build version
build_version.description: Deploy templates only: version of a successful build to deploy, e.g. 1.0.12. Empty: the newest successful build.

build_task_id.name: Build task
build_task_id.description: Deploy templates only: id of the build task to deploy (alternative to the version).

create_schedule.name: Create schedule
create_schedule.description: Creates a new cron schedule for a template in Semaphore. Response: id and name of the new schedule.

cron.name: Cron expression
cron.description: Five fields: minute hour day month weekday, e.g. "0 3 * * 1" (Mondays 3 am). Time zone as configured in Semaphore.

name.name: Name
name.description: Name of the schedule (default: name of the template).

active.name: Active
active.description: Switch the schedule on right away.

run_at.name: Run once at
run_at.description: One-time schedule: date and time (in the time zone of Home Assistant). Instead of "Cron expression".

delete_after_run.name: Delete after run
delete_after_run.description: Delete the schedule in Semaphore after it ran.

update_schedule.name: Change schedule
update_schedule.description: Changes cron expression, name, template or on/off of a schedule. Fields you leave out stay as they are.

template_id.name: Template id
template_id.description: Move the schedule to another template (id in Semaphore).

run_at.name: Run once at
run_at.description: One-time schedule: date and time (in the time zone of Home Assistant). Instead of "Cron expression".

delete_after_run.name: Delete after run
delete_after_run.description: Delete the schedule in Semaphore after it ran.

delete_schedule.name: Delete schedule
delete_schedule.description: Deletes the schedule in Semaphore. This cannot be undone.

init.title: New API token
init.description:
Semaphore ({url}) rejected the API token for the project “{project}” (HTTP 401). Until then the devices of this project are “unavailable”. You can enter a new token here.

In Semaphore create a new token under your user name (top right) → “API tokens” and enter it here - or enter a user name and password and the integration creates the token itself. It is checked before it is saved. Address: {url}, project: “{project}”.

data.store_login: Keep the user name and password to replace a rejected token by itself in future

data_description.store_login: Optional. The password is then kept - like the token - encrypted in the configuration of Home Assistant. Without the tick only the new token is stored.

unreachable.title: Semaphore is not reachable
unreachable.description:
Since {since} Home Assistant has not received an answer from Semaphore ({url}, project “{project}”): {detail}

The devices and entities of this project are “unavailable” meanwhile. Schedules and runs in Semaphore are not affected. Check that Semaphore is running (e.g. the Docker container), that the address is right and that network and firewall allow access. As soon as Semaphore answers again this notice disappears by itself.

project_missing.title: Semaphore project not found
project_missing.description: Since {since} Semaphore ({url}) answers for the project “{project}” with {detail}: the project was deleted or the API token may not (or no longer) see it. Check the project and the rights of the token in Semaphore. If the project was deleted, remove this entry under “Settings → Devices & services”. This notice disappears by itself as soon as the project is reachable again.

confirm.title: Replace the API token now
confirm.description:
The API token of the integration for the project “{project}” ({url}) expires on {when} (days left: {days}). After that Semaphore rejects it and the devices are “unavailable”. The automatic renewal is switched off (options of the integration). “Fix” creates a new token now.

A new token is created with the current one (same lifetime), checked and adopted. The old token stays in Semaphore and expires by itself. Address: {url}, project: “{project}”.
